title: Troubleshooting Applications and Container Logs

header.html: Manage and evaluate container output streams (plus the application break-and-fix tasks that appear throughout the domain)

toc.title: The method: top-down, one command at a time
Pod status words and what they mean
Break-and-fix catalog (all executed in this module's labs)

html:
1The method: top-down, one command at a time

Never guess. Follow the evidence from the outside in:

  1. What is the state? k get pods -o wide (STATUS, READY, RESTARTS, NODE).
  2. What does Kubernetes say? k describe pod <p>: read the Events at the bottom, then State, Last State, Reason, Exit Code.
  3. What did the app say? k logs <p> (and --previous).
  4. Is it the object or the node? Check the Deployment (k get deploy, k rollout status), then the node (Module 12).
  5. Fix, then verify with the same command that showed the problem.

k get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp -n <ns> lists recent events in time order across the namespace. Use -A for all namespaces.

2Pod status words and what they mean

STATUS Meaning First command Usual fix
Pending not scheduled, or waiting for a volume describe pod (FailedScheduling) resources, selector, taint, PVC (Modules 6, 10)
ContainerCreating scheduled, but the container cannot be set up describe pod events missing ConfigMap/Secret/PVC; CNI or image problem
ErrImagePull / ImagePullBackOff cannot pull the image describe pod ("Failed to pull image") wrong image name or tag, private registry needs an image pull Secret
CrashLoopBackOff container starts and exits repeatedly logs --previous, describe (exit code) bad command, missing env/config, failing dependency, wrong probe
CreateContainerError, RunContainerError runtime cannot start the process describe pod wrong command (executable not found), bad mount
Init:0/1, Init:Error an init container has not finished logs <p> -c <init> the thing it waits for does not exist yet
Error, OOMKilled container died describe (Last State: Reason, Exit Code) OOMKilled = memory limit too low (exit 137)
Running but 0/1 ready readiness probe failing describe (Readiness probe failed) wrong probe port/path or app not up
Terminating for a long time finalizer or node down describe, node state force delete only as a last step

Exit codes: 0 normal, 1 application error, 137 killed (OOM or SIGKILL), 143 terminated by SIGTERM.

3Reading logs: every variant

k logs web-1                          # one container
k logs web-1 -c side                  # a named container (required when the Pod has several)
k logs web-1 --previous               # the last crashed instance: the error is here
k logs web-1 -f --tail=20             # follow, last 20 lines
k logs web-1 --since=10m              # last ten minutes
k logs deploy/web                     # one Pod of the Deployment (a single Pod is picked)
k logs -l app=svc --tail=-1           # every Pod with the label, all lines
k logs -l app=svc --tail=-1 --prefix  # each line prefixed with the Pod name
k logs -n kube-system kube-apiserver-<node>
  • Multi-container Pods: k logs <pod> with no -c prints only one container (the first one, or the one named in the kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container annotation) and a "Defaulted container" notice. Always name the container with -c when the task names one (Lab 11.1). k get pod <p> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].name}' lists them; init containers are in .spec.initContainers.
  • --tail with a selector defaults to 10 lines per Pod; use --tail=-1 for all lines (Lab 11.9).
  • A crash loop's real message is in --previous. The current container may have no output yet (Lab 11.2). In the lab cluster --previous sometimes answers "unable to retrieve container logs" (the old container was already cleaned up); then plain k logs <pod> shows the same message, because the app prints it on every attempt.
  • Logs are the container's stdout and stderr. A path inside the container is read with k exec <p> -- cat /path.

4Break-and-fix catalog (all executed in this module's labs)

Symptom Cause found by Fix
ImagePullBackOff (Lab 11.3) describe pod: "manifest unknown" or "not found" k set image deploy/web nginx=nginx:alpine
CrashLoopBackOff, log says "DB_HOST is required" (Lab 11.4) k logs k set env deploy/worker DB_HOST=db.internal
ContainerCreating, event "configmap ... not found" (Lab 11.5) describe pod (FailedMount) create the ConfigMap; the kubelet retries and the Pod starts by itself, no delete needed
OOMKilled, restarts (Lab 11.6) describe: Last State Reason OOMKilled, exit 137 raise resources.limits.memory; recreate the Pod (Pod resources are immutable)
Init:0/1 (Lab 11.7) logs <pod> -c <init>: "waiting for db" create the missing Service or dependency
CreateContainerError (Lab 11.8) event: "executable file not found in $PATH" fix the command (typo sleeep)
Pod with wrong probe (Lab 5.9) describe: Liveness probe failed correct the probe
Pending (Labs 6.8, 10.6, 10.7) FailedScheduling events resources, class name, access mode

Editing rules: a Pod's image can be changed in place with k set image (and k edit), but most other Pod fields cannot: delete and recreate (use --force --grace-period 0 to avoid waiting). For Deployments, edit the template and the rollout replaces the Pods.

5Useful debugging tools

k exec -it web-1 -- sh                              # shell inside the container
k exec web-1 -- env                                 # environment as the container sees it
k run dbg --rm -it --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never -- sh   # throw-away debug Pod
k debug web-1 -it --image=busybox:1.36 --target=main            # ephemeral debug container in a running Pod
k port-forward pod/web-1 8080:80                    # test a Pod from your terminal
k get pod web-1 -o yaml                             # full spec and status
k auth can-i ...                                    # permission problems

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m11 -->

Lab 11.1: container logs

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-01-container-logs)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace lg1, the Pod multi has two containers, app and side. Save the log output of the container side (only that container) to ~/answers/side.log on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n lg1 logs multi
kubectl -n lg1 logs multi -c side > ~/answers/side.log
cat ~/answers/side.log

Lab 11.2: previous logs

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-02-previous-logs)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace lg2, the Pod crashy keeps restarting. Find the error message the application prints just before it exits and save that one line, exactly as printed, to ~/answers/error.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n lg2 get pod crashy
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  out=$( (kubectl -n lg2 logs crashy --previous 2>/dev/null || kubectl -n lg2 logs crashy 2>/dev/null) | tail -1)
  case "$out" in ""|*"unable to retrieve"*|*"not found"*) sleep 4;; *) break;; esac
done
echo "$out" > ~/answers/error.txt
cat ~/answers/error.txt

Lab 11.3: fix image pull

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-03-fix-image-pull)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app3, the Deployment web (2 replicas) shows ImagePullBackOff. Find the cause and fix the Deployment so that both replicas run nginx:alpine.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n app3 describe pod -l app=web | grep -i -A3 "Failed to pull" | head -6
kubectl -n app3 set image deployment web nginx=nginx:alpine
kubectl -n app3 rollout status deployment web --timeout=120s

Lab 11.4: fix missing env

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-04-fix-missing-env)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app4, the Pods of the Deployment worker crash with a clear message in their logs. Read the log, then fix the Deployment (do not change the image or the command) so that the Pods run stably with the required setting DB_HOST=db.internal.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n app4 logs deploy/worker --tail=3
kubectl -n app4 set env deployment worker DB_HOST=db.internal
kubectl -n app4 rollout status deployment worker --timeout=120s

Lab 11.5: fix missing configmap

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-05-fix-missing-configmap)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app5, the Pod site is stuck in ContainerCreating. Find out why (read the events) and fix it without deleting the Pod: the Pod needs a ConfigMap site-config whose key index.html contains Hello from config, mounted at /usr/share/nginx/html.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n app5 describe pod site | grep -i -A3 "FailedMount"
kubectl -n app5 create configmap site-config --from-literal=index.html='Hello from config'
kubectl -n app5 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/site --timeout=180s

Lab 11.6: oomkilled

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-06-oomkilled)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app6, the Pod hungry restarts all the time. Find the reason in the Pod's status. The container needs about 40 MiB of memory to run. Recreate the Pod hungry (same image and command) with a memory limit of 128Mi so that it runs stably with 0 restarts.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n app6 get pod hungry -o jsonpath='{.status.containerStatuses[0].lastState.terminated.reason}'; echo
kubectl -n app6 delete pod hungry --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n app6 apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: hungry}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sh", "-c", "x=$(yes | head -c 40000000); echo allocated; sleep 3600"]
    resources:
      limits: {memory: 128Mi}
Y
kubectl -n app6 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/hungry --timeout=120s
sleep 15

Lab 11.7: fix init container

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-07-fix-init-container)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app7, the Pod api is stuck in Init:0/1: its init container waits until the DNS name db resolves inside the namespace. Without changing the Pod, make the Pod start. The name db must be the name of a Service in app7 that selects the existing Pod database (label app=database, nginx on port 80).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n app7 get pod api
kubectl -n app7 logs api -c wait-db --tail=3
kubectl -n app7 expose pod database --name=db --port=80
kubectl -n app7 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/api --timeout=180s

Lab 11.8: fix wrong command

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-08-fix-wrong-command)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace app8, the Deployment ticker cannot start its container (the status shows an error such as CreateContainerError or RunContainerError). Find the cause in the Pod events and fix the Deployment so that 2 replicas run. The container is supposed to run the command sleep 3600.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n app8 describe pod -l app=ticker | grep -i -E "executable file not found|Error" | head -3
kubectl -n app8 patch deployment ticker --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/command","value":["sleep","3600"]}]'
kubectl -n app8 rollout status deployment ticker --timeout=120s

Lab 11.9: logs by label

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m11-09-logs-by-label)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace lg9, the Deployment svc has 3 Pods (label app=svc). Each Pod printed one line starting with ERROR at startup, among other lines. Collect the ERROR lines of all three Pods into ~/answers/errors.txt on the host (one line per Pod, no other lines).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n lg9 logs -l app=svc --tail=-1 | grep '^ERROR' > ~/answers/errors.txt
cat ~/answers/errors.txt

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1Where do you find the error of a container that is in CrashLoopBackOff?

Show the answer

In kubectl logs <pod> --previous and the exit code in kubectl describe pod.

R2What does exit code 137 and OOMKilled indicate?

Show the answer

The container was killed for exceeding its memory limit.

R3A Pod has two containers. How do you read the second one's logs?

Show the answer

kubectl logs <pod> -c <container-name>.

R4How do you read the logs of all Pods with a label, all lines?

Show the answer

kubectl logs -l key=value --tail=-1.

R5A Pod is stuck in ContainerCreating and the event says the ConfigMap is not found. What do you do?

Show the answer

Create the ConfigMap; the kubelet retries and the Pod starts.

R6Which command lists namespace events in time order?

Show the answer

kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp.

R7What does Init:0/1 mean and where do you look?

Show the answer

The first of one init container has not finished; read kubectl logs <pod> -c <init-container>.

R8Can you edit the resource limits of a running Pod?

Show the answer

No; delete and recreate it (or change the Deployment template).

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Method get, describe (Events), logs, then fix and verify
Image problems ImagePullBackOff -> tag or name; describe pod
Crashes logs --previous; exit 137 = OOM; 1 = app error
Stuck creating missing ConfigMap, Secret, PVC; read events
Logs -c container, --previous, -l selector with --tail=-1, -f, --since
Init containers logs -c <init>; waits for a dependency
Immutable Pod resources/commands: recreate; Deployments: edit the template
